learning_objective: 🎯 Understand what India buys from and sells to the world, how trade policies have changed, and the role of major sea ports!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Before independence, India exported raw materials and imported finished goods. Today, India exports manufactured goods, engineering items, gems, and IT services, while importing heavy machinery and crude oil.
India's biggest import bill comes from Petroleum (crude oil), gold, capital goods (machinery), and electronic components. High imports lead to a trade deficit.
Major exports include Engineering goods, Gems and Jewellery, Chemicals, Agricultural products (rice, spices), and Textiles. We trade heavily with the USA, UAE, and China.

India has a long coastline with 12 major and roughly 200 minor ports. Major west coast ports (Mumbai, Kandla, Kochi) handle trade with Europe/Middle East. East coast ports (Chennai, Kolkata, Visakhapatnam) face Southeast Asia.
A hinterland is the area behind a port that it serves. It collects goods from this area to export, and distributes imported goods into this area. A rich hinterland makes a rich port.

fun_activity.title: 📦 The Global House
fun_activity.instructions: Find three items in your home that are imported (look at electronics or toys). Now, research one Indian product that is famous worldwide (like Darjeeling Tea or Indian spices). You just explored import and export!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly define 'Hinterland'—this is a classic definition question.
📌 Be able to locate all 12 major ports on an outline map of India.
📌 Know why Kandla port was developed (to relieve pressure on Mumbai port after the loss of Karachi port during partition).
quick_recap: ⭐ India has a negative balance of trade because the value of its imports (mainly crude oil) exceeds its exports.
⭐ Mumbai is the largest natural port in India.
⭐ Visakhapatnam is the deepest landlocked and protected port on the eastern coast.
